title: My son was born a week ago, and today I launched my first solo game: a puzzle game where you sort cut-up songs by ear
author: SalamanderEast7639
selftext:
Hearsay is out on Steam today.

Every recording in a basement archive has been cut into unlabeled tapes. You play a tape, work out which of ten genre cabinets it belongs in, and shelve the pieces in the order you hear them. A full set checks itself like Wordle: green is right, yellow is the right recording in the wrong slot, orange is the right cabinet but the wrong set, and red is the wrong cabinet.

164 recordings, from 100-year-old Library of Congress records to jazz, horror and video game music. No timer, no fail state.

A curator played it last week and told me exactly what was frustrating. In the final days before launch I added the orange color, locked in green tapes, made the hint system cheap and early, and cleaned up the wording. Feedback like that made the game better, so if you play it, I’d love to hear yours.

It’s 20% off for launch week, and there’s a free demo if you want to try it first.

AI disclosure: I used an AI coding assistant for help with programming. There’s no AI art, music or voice: the art is purchased, the old recordings are real Library of Congress archives, and the modern music is by human artists, credited in the game.

The AI helped with code and testing. Every design call, including the ones from that curator’s feedback, was mine.

Steam: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5274720/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5274720/)
